title: Type streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart's two catch blocks to Exception — bare Object catches swallow Error subtypes as warnings
why: Neither catch has an `on X` clause, so both also catch Dart Error subtypes (NoSuchMethodError, TypeError, RangeError, StateError) that signal genuine programming bugs, not recoverable runtime conditions — exactly what EH-4 says never to catch. A bug in StreakStateProvider or an unexpected state shape gets downgraded to a single logger.warning(...) call (not even error/critical) and the loop or stream quietly continues or ends — no crash, no Crashlytics report, nothing but a line in a 2000-entry ring buffer nobody reviews outside 'Send Diagnostic Logs'. This provider runs unconditionally in the app shell every session (per its own doc comment), so a regression here has zero blast-radius signal to catch it.
recommendation: Narrow both catches to `on Exception catch (e, st)` (or the specific exception types StreakStateProvider/AnalyticsService can throw) and let Error subtypes propagate to the zone's onError handler like the rest of the app.
acceptance_criteria: Both catch clauses in streak_milestone_analytics_observer.dart use `on Exception catch` (or a named typed exception), not bare `catch (e, st)`
streak_milestone_analytics_observer_test.dart's existing R6-3 tests still pass unchanged (they throw plain Exception, not Error)

corrections: Ran a probe test: querying a closed Drift NativeDatabase throws StateError (e is Error==true, e is Exception==false) — the exact scenario R6-3's stream-error test triggers via db.close(). Narrowing line 83's catch to `on Exception` lets that StateError escape and flips state.hasError to true, breaking the existing green test the finding claims 'still pass unchanged.' Doc comment (lines 34-37) also documents the swallow-all behavior as deliberate, not accidental. Downgrading severity/confidence accordingly; the inner catch (line 74) is a cleaner, lower-stakes instance of the same rule violation.
